newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, Wednsday March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, Wednsday March 5.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The bomb discovered near the offices of Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army, in Monaghan on Monday contained enough explosive to have wrecked part of the town.
- In the absence of any significant political progress, the Stormont multi-party peace talks are to be adjourned on Wednesday until after the British general election.

- A furious row has broken out over comments made by small business group Irish Small and Medium Enterprises (ISME), who said that many of the unemployed were "social misfits" and that FAS courses were turning people into social junkies.
- A fundamentally different approach to determining the pay of chief exectives of commerical State companies is to be introduced by the Irish government.
- Irish police in County Donegal have issued an urgent warning to parents after the attempted abduction of two young schoolgirls on Monday night.

- A member of the Irish Republican Army who escaped from Portlaoise prison in County Laois 23 years ago was back behind bars in the top security jail on Tuesday night, being recaptured by Irish police.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton has been warned to expect significant cuts in Ireland's share of the EU structural funds.

- Division between Irish Minister for Arts and Culture, Michael D.Higgins, and the Democratic Left Party of Ireland's rainbow coalition have forced the postponement beyond the Irish general election of a plan to set up a new 'super-authority' to govern Ireland's national broadcasting station RTE.
